summary: The routine-eligibility producer closure is five files (.fsgg/routine-development.json, the workflow, check-claim-generation.py, the envelope, lib/gate.py). A receiver is judged by the copy in its own base because the workflow is pull_request_target, so a receiver on an old copy keeps refusing moved bases and push parents until it adopts a fixed set; the adopting PR cannot prove itself. The set is adopted whole (a mixed old/new set breaks, #5191 review F2) from the FS.GG.Drivers workspace payload that workspace-inventory.json already lists, not by hand copy; the published 0.114.3 payload equalled canonical, and ten receivers matched it after adoption. Observed on 2026-11-01: some receivers also pin the workflow's sha256 in their own registries. FS.GG.Coordination's immutable execution-pin extension refused the new workflow until that one entry was rehashed (derived edit in the adoption PR). FS.GG.Rendering's original-tag settlement fences pin it for the unsettled 0.32.4 subject, so adoption there is held: re-pinning would rebind that original effect's custody. scripts/routine-closure.py (apply, check, sweep) names such pins as stale-pin by comparing 64-hex tokens with earlier revisions of the five files; a historical-record file must be waived explicitly. Scope: observation of these two receivers on 2026-11-01; other receivers may add pins, and the check needs full .github history.
title: Receivers adopt the routine-eligibility closure atomically, and repo-local digest pins can block the adoption
